      Jerich-go on this tour!
      This was a really nice tour with Lahdo. Particular highlights for me were going to the Jordan River baptismal site (there was a group there with music playing while we were there and it was a really nice atmosphere) and being able to go to the grotto of the Church of the Nativity on Christmas Eve. Interesting to see Jericho and Ramallah for the first time for me too. Full marks to Lahdo for being positive and friendly throughout, and for keeping the tour ticking along to schedule. Lunch was good too - I was anticipating we'd be in a restaurant but got a nice home-cooked meal in a place with a good view. I would add that I was relieved that this wasn't an overtly political tour, as I'm not particularly attracted to that side of things compared to historical stuff, and no agenda was pushed or anything. I wasn't personally that interested in seeing the graffiti on the wall in Bethlehem, but of course I recognise it's a part of the current situation to know about, and was just a short walk at the end of the tour.

      Hiking and soaking, great day
      Outstanding day! We left crazy early to get to Masasa, and walked up the snake trail in the dark to see sunrise. After sunrise had just under an hour to walk around on top before heading back on foot. If you walk any mountain paths you should be able to do this, there's no altitude. Then a brief stop at Ein Geri nature center, no 2nd mountain you have to do but some short stair climbs, make sure you see all 3 waterfalls. Number 3 is the best! The Dead Sea is an experience you should do. Float and get in the mud and rinse off. Shmuel is great at this, he gets you there and tells you everything you need to know and reminds you of the schedule so you get back in time for everything else. You can leave your stuff on the bus so you only take what you need for that part of the trip. Bring some water for the day, can refill before and after Ein Gedi. This is an active trip with transport and instruction before each place, but no hand-holding during. Very happy we chose this trip, the scheduling and execution were both A+
      Written March 9, 2025

    Chicago, Illinois388 contributions

    This one we loved! Great scenery, and Mar Saba and Sacheed

    Dec 2019 • Family
    Okay I'd like to say that every Abraham Tour is terrific, but they're actually very varied though always reasonable. However this one, we loved. It would be hard to do this tour yourself and might not even be safe depending on the condition of the terrain. Besides you'd miss the real insight into the Bedouins that Sacheed provided. He's great. As for Mar Saba...what an unexpected marvel in a spectacular setting! Truly one of the most fabulous sights I saw in Israel...up there with some of the world's more well-known landmarks. Set in an isolated hillside in the Negev desert this ancient Greek Orthodox monastery is a wonderful to behold. The color blends in with the curved landscape... part cave-dwelling part ancient ruins and part magnificent multi-layer structure climbing the hillside. Its presence seems positively mystical. The best view is from the israeli-controlled West Bank (I believe it's area C) if you off road into the desert, past Bedouin lean-to houses and long floppy-eared goats and young herders on their donkeys. But if you want to enter the monastery, and women can't, you have to do that from the palestinian-controlled side. Don't miss it! Wadi Qelt was also lovely although it was a little cold for a swim, you can put your feet in and then have the small fish peck at the dead skin. You can also watch local rock climbers scale the canyon. I do wish we had a little more time the climb up to the small monastery and hike. I think they could have added an hour to the tour and gotten us back at 4.
    Written January 3, 2020
